display.title: Episode 522: A Judge for a Day, Chapter 2
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi explains Tzivos Hashem's mitzvah missions and leads Tehillim for the Rebbe, a class says the Shema, and a children's make-believe trial solves the mystery of the 365 gold coins.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi describes the fun and purpose of being a soldier in Tzivos Hashem: mitzvah missions that build character, teach children to share their Yiddishkeit with friends and relatives at every Yom Tov, and earn points and ranks. The Rebbe founded Tzivos Hashem ten years earlier and takes great pleasure in every child who joins; now, while the Rebbe needs a complete recovery, children can help by doing their missions, enrolling friends and praying. Everyone recites Tehillim chapter 20 together, then joins the Hakochainik march in the joy of Adar. A class from a Brooklyn girls' school recites the Shema, and listeners give tzedakah. 'A Judge for a Day' concludes: Leib discovers a peephole in the thin wall between the butcher's and the tailor's shops. The puzzled judge, strolling in the park, watches children act out the case. Their little judge drops the coins into warm water: oil from the butcher's greasy hands rises to the surface, proving the money is Beryl's. The real judge repeats the test in court, and the boy, Leib, grows up to be the great Torah scholar known as the Shaagas Aryeh.
display.lesson: Hashem answers sincere prayer, and a child who uses his wisdom to help someone in trouble can do great things.

date.note: 'We are still in the month of Adar'; continues the story begun in episode 521 (24 March 1992); the next episode (523) is in Nissan.
